overview.summary: Hash Maps store data in key-value pairs, providing average O(1) time complexity for lookups, insertions, and deletions.
learningObjectives: Understand the concept of a hashing function.
Explain how key-value pairs are stored and retrieved.
Understand hash collisions and basic resolution techniques.
overview.interviewRelevance: Hash maps are the ultimate 'cheat code' in interviews. Whenever you need to optimize a lookup from O(n) to O(1), a hash map is usually the answer.

paragraphs: Imagine walking into a massive library and wanting a specific book. Instead of checking every shelf (which takes hours), you ask the librarian.
You give the librarian the title (the Key), and they instantly give you the exact aisle and shelf number (the Value). A Hash Map is your digital librarian.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: A hash function mathematically converts a key directly into a memory address, skipping the search entirely.

definition.technicalDefinition: A Hash Map (or Hash Table) is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values using a hash function.

vocabulary.definition: The unique identifier used to retrieve the value.
The data associated with the key.
An algorithm that converts a key into a specific array index.
When two different keys hash to the same exact index.

keyProperties: O(1) average time complexity for lookup, insert, and delete.
Keys must be unique and hashable (usually immutable).
Unordered data (unless using specific variants like LinkedHashMap).

metaphor: A coat check room. You hand in your coat (value), get a numbered ticket (hash of the key), and can retrieve it instantly later.
mentalModel.clickSentence: By trading space (memory) for time, we eliminate the need to search.

memoryDescription: Under the hood, a hash map is usually just an Array.
The Hash Function computes an index, and the key-value pair is stored at that specific index in the array.

steps.explanation: A hash map turns a key into a bucket index. Start with 5 empty buckets.
Bucket 2 is already taken — a collision. Chain "emu" onto the same bucket.
Bucket 2 is already taken — a collision. Chain "tac" onto the same bucket.
Lookup "dog": hash to bucket 4, scan its short chain → 7. Average O(1).

operations.name: Insert / Update
operations.description: Calculate the hash of the key, find the index, and store the value.
operations.visualNote: Instantly drops the value into the bucket.

operations.name: Lookup
operations.description: Calculate the hash of the key and retrieve the value at that index.
operations.visualNote: Instantly jumps to the bucket and retrieves.

patternTemplate.whenToUse: Whenever you are repeatedly searching an array for a value. Store values in a map as you go to turn O(n) lookups into O(1).
patternTemplate.spaceComplexity: O(n) memory to store the elements.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You have an array of integers. You need to check if there are two numbers that add up to a target sum. A nested loop takes O(n²). How can you do it in O(n)?
recognitionQuiz.explanation: As you iterate, store each number in a Hash Map. For each number, you can instantly check if `(target - current_number)` is already in the map.

examples.title: Two Sum
examples.problemStatement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
steps: If complement is in map, you found the pair!
Otherwise, add the current number and its index to the map.
examples.rationale: We trade O(n) space for O(1) lookups, dropping total time from O(n²) to O(n).

conceptQuiz.question: What is a Hash Collision?
options: When two different keys generate the exact same index in the underlying array.
When you try to look up a key that doesn't exist.
When the hash map runs out of memory.
When you delete a key while iterating.
conceptQuiz.explanation: Because the underlying array is smaller than the infinite possibilities of keys, eventually two keys will hash to the same slot.

conceptQuiz.question: Why is Hash Map lookup O(1) 'average' and not 'guaranteed'?
options: Because hash collisions might occur, requiring the map to check a short list of items at that index.
Because sometimes the computer CPU is busy.
Because memory addresses take time to calculate.
conceptQuiz.explanation: In the worst case (e.g., all keys collide to the exact same index), looking up a key degrades to O(n) as it searches through the collided list.

practice.title: Valid Anagram
practice.keyInsight: Count character frequencies using a hash map.

practice.title: Group Anagrams
practice.keyInsight: Use the sorted version of the string as the key in the hash map.
